name: reads-like-ai
query: draft-spec.md reads like ChatGPT wrote it. Fix it.
why: The diagnostic complaint phrasing is the primary trigger.

name: de-slop-the-doc
query: De-slop draft-spec.md before I send it to the client.
why: Direct request in the skill's own vocabulary, with a ship-it deadline.

name: cringe-prose
query: Go through draft-spec.md and take out the corny AI voice, the hedging and the em dashes. Keep what it actually says.
why: Names three categories and states the preserve-meaning invariant without naming the skill.

name: review-generated-prose-for-inventions
query: An agent wrote draft-spec.md. Check it for anything it made up or contradicted itself on, and tidy the writing.
why: Pass 2 is half the skill. Reviewing model output for hallucinations and contradictions must trigger it, not only the prose polish.

name: polish-before-shipping
query: I drafted draft-spec.md with an LLM. Make it sound like a person wrote it.
why: Model-drafted text plus a humanise request.

name: not-a-rewrite-request
query: Rewrite draft-spec.md to argue for a database instead of a queue.
why: Changing what a document argues is explicitly out of scope. Same file, opposite intent, so this isolates intent from file presence.

name: not-a-code-refactor
query: This function is ugly and hard to follow. Clean it up.
why: Code logic is out of scope. 'Clean it up' alone must not fire this skill.

name: not-ui-slop
query: This landing page looks like every other AI-generated site. Make it less generic.
why: Precision boundary against the sibling skill: frontend-aesthetics should fire instead. Visual slop is that skill, prose slop is this one, and both complaints use 'AI-generated'.

name: not-a-fresh-draft
query: Write me a blog post about Iceberg table formats.
why: Authoring from scratch is not an eraser pass.
